report: First-ever Demonology activation removed old spells and auto-placed new ones, but those buttons vanished after restart. User confirmed manually arranged specializations survive switching normally.
evidence: The affected active spec1 had only two saved character_action rows, unlike populated specs0 and2. This is a saved-state snapshot, not a complete packet trace of the original switch.
ActivateTalentGroup saves outgoing actions, learns incoming spells with automatic placement, then queries the destination actions. Previously _LoadActions only ran for a nonempty query.

An empty destination inherited outgoing UNCHANGED/CHANGED action states; _SaveActions therefore skipped or UPDATEd rows absent from the destination. For a populated destination, _LoadActions cleared newly auto-added spells.
The character_action.action column and save handlers use uint64, but the load handler narrowed IDs with GetUInt32.
change: Always load destination actions after spec learning. During this spec-only load, capture pending actions first. Empty destinations copy valid pending buttons into fresh NEW rows; populated destinations keep saved slots and merge only pending new/changed spells through the existing auto-placement helper. Ordinary login does not merge previous in-memory bars. Read full64-bit action IDs.
automated_checks: Test-ActionBarPersistence.ps1 extracts production ActionButton state management and Add/Remove/Load/Save handlers. A statement-aware database fixture distinguishes INSERT from UPDATE-on-missing, tests first activation, retained shared spell/macro, old-spec rejection, existing custom macro/item positions, new/changed spells, duplicates, save/relog, repeated loads, deletion, same-spec replacement and destination isolation. The spell-classification helper is stubbed to its duplicate/empty-slot contract; its native DB2 classification is not verified by this harness.
